title: Stovetop mac and cheese
skill: Roux, then béchamel, then cheese sauce

notes.text: For more than 8, make the sauce in the large pot after draining the pasta, so it all fits.

move.title: Butter, flour, milk, cheese
move.body: A roux is butter and flour cooked together. It's the start of many sauces and gravies. Today you'll make one, whisk milk into it to make a smooth white sauce called béchamel, then melt cheese into that for a creamy cheese sauce. Stir in the macaroni and you have real mac and cheese.

why.title: Why cook the flour in butter
why.body: Raw flour tastes like paste. A couple of minutes of bubbling in butter cooks away that taste. The butter also coats each bit of flour, so when the milk goes in, the flour spreads out evenly instead of clumping into lumps.

why.title: How flour thickens milk
why.body: Flour is full of starch. When the milk gets hot, the starch grains soak up liquid and swell, like tiny sponges. Millions of swollen grains turn thin milk into a thick, smooth sauce. It only happens once the sauce bubbles, so keep whisking until it does.

why.title: Milk a little at a time
why.body: The first splash of milk turns the roux into a thick paste. Whisk it smooth, then add more. Smooth at every step means smooth at the end. Dump all the milk in at once and lumps can hide in it.

why.title: Cheese goes in off the heat
why.body: Cheese that boils turns grainy and oily as its fat separates out. Turning off the heat first lets the hot sauce melt the cheese gently, so it stays smooth.

wrong.fix: Whisk hard for a minute. If lumps are still there, pour the sauce through a strainer and keep going.
Keep it bubbling gently and whisking for a few more minutes. It thickens as it cooks.

wrong.sign: The cheese sauce looks grainy or oily
wrong.fix: It got too hot. Take it off the heat and whisk in a splash of cold milk.

wrong.sign: The mac and cheese got thick and stiff
wrong.fix: Stir in a little warm milk until it's creamy again. Pasta keeps soaking up sauce as it sits.

quiz.explain: A roux is butter and flour cooked together. It thickens sauces and gravies.

quiz.q: Why turn off the heat before adding the cheese?
choices: Boiling makes cheese grainy and oily
quiz.explain: Gentle heat keeps the cheese sauce smooth.

substitutions.note: Start checking it 2 minutes early. Gluten-free pasta turns soft fast.

steps.text: Fill the large pot with the water, add the salt for the pasta, cover it, and set it over high heat to come to a boil.
steps.tip: Fill the pot at the sink, then carry it to the stove before it's hot. Never carry a pot of boiling water.

steps.text: Measure the milk, flour, cheese, and seasonings, and set them next to the stove.
steps.tip: A sauce moves fast once it starts. Have everything ready first.

steps.text: When the water is boiling hard, add the macaroni and stir. Boil it 1 minute less than the box says, stirring now and then.
steps.tip: It cooks a little more in the sauce, so take it out while it's still a bit firm.

steps.text: Turn off the stove under the pasta. Set the colander in the sink and carefully pour the macaroni into it, tipping the pot away from you. Leave it in the colander.
steps.tip: The steam rushes up when you pour. Keep your face back, and pour slowly.

steps.text: Melt the butter in the saucepan over medium heat. Sprinkle in the flour and whisk until it's a smooth paste. Keep whisking while it bubbles gently.
steps.look: A smooth, bubbling paste the color of pale sand. If it turns brown, the heat is too high.
steps.tip: Whisk into the corners of the pan, where the roux likes to hide.

steps.text: Pour in about a cup of the milk and whisk hard. It'll go thick and lumpy, then smooth. Add the rest of the milk a little at a time, whisking smooth after each pour.
steps.tip: Pour slowly, close to the pan, so the hot roux doesn't splatter.

steps.text: Keep whisking, scraping the bottom, until the sauce bubbles gently and gets thick. That's béchamel.
steps.look: It coats the back of a spoon. Run your finger across the spoon: the line stays clear.

steps.text: Turn off the heat. Stir in the cheese a handful at a time, letting each one melt before the next. Stir in {qty:salt} salt, the garlic powder, the mustard if you're using it, and a few grinds of pepper.
steps.look: Smooth, glossy, and orange-yellow, with no strings or oil.

steps.text: Pour the macaroni back into the large pot and pour the cheese sauce over it. Stir until every piece is coated.
Taste a piece, after letting it cool, and add a pinch more salt if it needs it. Serve right away.
steps.tip: If it thickens while it waits, stir in a splash of warm milk.
